content:
As Leo just mentioned in his Lean Together 2025 keynote, we are starting the Lean Kernel Arena.

The goal is to give more visibility to our ecosystem of external checkers and test and compare them.

On https://arena.lean-lang.org/ you’ll find a table summarizing the existing checkers: The official kernel, two experimental PRs against it, @Chris Bailey ’s nanoda, @Mario Carneiro's lean4lean and a few non-serious checkers to test the arena.

The arena runs them against a variety of tests: Some plain exports (Init.Prelude, Init, Std, mathlib), a (still small) number of bad proofs that ought to be rejected, and a (still incomplete) sequence of “tutorial” tests that provide guidance when writing a new checkers.

One hope is that the arena will incentivise further lean checker development. Do you have an itch to write a lean kernel? Maybe with a different angle to term representation, type checking or host language? Or maybe you like citing the stats that the arena provides in your PL paper?

It doesn't even have to be a complete one to start with, your checker can “decline” tests that are not supported and it will not be counted against you.

Or do you rather enjoy poking holes into other people’s code? Then maybe you want to contribute interesting tests!

See the repository README for more information on writing checkers and tests.

I’ve labeled the arena as “under construction” for now, until at least

  • the ongoing revision of the export format has settled and all relevant tools (lean4export’s pretty-printer and parser, nanoda’s parser) have been updated
  • the next Lean release is out, and checkers had time to update to the latest Lean prelude definitions.

That should not stop you from playing around with it right now! Just don’t take the statistics too serious just yet.

Discussion welcome at #general > Lean Kernel Arena
